description: Trunk soft-tissue and surface-anatomy dimensions: shoulder breadth and slope, chest morphology, abdominal shape and definition, waist definition, back morphology, navel morphology. Captures the per-region detail that body-shape.json's whole-body composite metrics do not. Dimensions draw from sports-medicine, body-contouring, and aesthetic-anatomy literature.

dimensions.scale_citation: Aligned with anthropometry references on biacromial breadth as a primary frame-size dimension.
dimensions.description: Width across the shoulders relative to overall body proportions.

values.definition: Shoulders narrow relative to hips.
Shoulders proportional.
Pronounced shoulder breadth; characteristic V-shape silhouette in lean subjects.

dimensions.scale_citation: Aligned with descriptors used in tailoring and artistic-anatomy literature.
dimensions.description: Angle of the shoulders from the base of the neck outward.

values.definition: Shoulders nearly horizontal; minimal slope.
Average shoulder slope.
Substantial downward slope from neck base.

dimensions.scale_citation: Aligned with descriptors used in thoracic-surgery and pectus-deformity literature.

values.definition: Anterior chest wall approximately flat in profile.
Standard anterior chest contour.
Increased anteroposterior chest diameter.
Visible sternal depression.
Visible sternal protrusion ('pigeon chest').

dimensions.scale_citation: Aligned with sports-medicine descriptors of pectoral musculature.
dimensions.description: Visible pectoral muscle definition in subjects with apparent male physiognomy.

values.definition: Pectorals not visible as discrete landmarks.
Pectorals visible but not prominently defined.
Clear pectoral definition; visible separation between pectoralis and surrounding tissue.
Pronounced pectoral mass and definition.
Subject not in male physiognomy or chest not visible.

dimensions.scale_citation: Aligned with body-contouring and abdominoplasty literature.

values.definition: Abdominal wall sits posterior to the rib cage / pelvis line.
Abdominal wall in plane with rib cage / pelvis.
Subtle anterior protrusion.
Clearly protruding abdomen.

dimensions.scale_citation: Aligned with sports-medicine and bodybuilding descriptors of rectus abdominis visibility.

values.definition: No visible muscular definition.
Minor definition visible at the upper abdomen only.
Upper rectus abdominis visible; lower abdomen smooth.
Full rectus abdominis visible plus inscriptional definition between segments.

dimensions.scale_citation: Aligned with body-contouring literature on the waist as a perceptual axis.
dimensions.description: Visible waist taper between the rib cage and the pelvis.

values.definition: No visible waist; rib cage to pelvis nearly straight.
Slight inward curve at waist.
Clear waist taper.
Strong hourglass-equivalent waist definition.

dimensions.scale_citation: Aligned with sports-medicine and aesthetic-anatomy descriptors of dorsal-trunk silhouette.

values.definition: Wide upper back tapering to narrow waist.
Approximately equal upper-back and waist breadth.
Wider at hip/waist than upper back.

dimensions.scale_citation: Aligned with descriptors used in posture-assessment literature; subset of the body-shape posture dimension at higher granularity.

values.definition: Reduced lumbar curve; flattened lower back.
Standard lumbar lordosis.
Substantial lumbar curve; sometimes called sway-back.

dimensions.scale_citation: Aligned with descriptors used in abdominoplasty and umbilicoplasty literature on umbilical aesthetics.
dimensions.description: Shape and orientation of the navel.

values.definition: Long axis vertical; common aesthetic reference.
Umbilicus projects outward from abdominal plane.

dimensions.scale_citation: Aligned with sports-medicine descriptors of midline-tendon visibility.
dimensions.description: Visibility of the linea alba — the central midline tendon between the two rectus abdominis muscles.

values.definition: Visible under tension only.
Clear vertical midline visible at rest.
Pronounced midline; common with very low body-fat percentage.

references: Lockwood TE (1991). Superficial fascial system (SFS) of the trunk and extremities. Plastic and Reconstructive Surgery, 87(6).
Pollock H, Pollock T (2000). Progressive tension sutures: a technique to reduce local complications in abdominoplasty. Plastic and Reconstructive Surgery, 105(7).
Standring S (ed.) (2020). Gray's Anatomy: The Anatomical Basis of Clinical Practice, 42nd Edition. Elsevier.
